Method of Attack: Injecting malicious JavaScript into hacked websites via compromised WordPress sites
Loading Binance Smart Chain (BSC) JS library and fetching malicious scripts from the blockchain
Injecting script tags into webpages to load malicious code from blockchain
Triggering download of third-stage payload from attacker-controlled C2 servers
Displaying fake browser update overlays to trick users into downloading malware
Using blockchain smart contracts to host malicious code making it unblockable and takedown-resistant
Discoverer: Guardio Labs researchers Nati Tal and Oleg Zaytsev
Impacted Systems: User browsers (Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox)
Attack Vector: Compromised WordPress sites with injected script tags
Blockchain smart contracts on Binance Smart Chain (BSC) hosting malicious scripts
Malicious executable downloads from Dropbox and other legitimate hosting sites
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious smart contract addresses on Binance Smart Chain (BSC)
Script injections loading BSC JS library
Fake browser update overlays on hacked websites
Third-stage payload downloads from attacker C2 servers
Malicious executables hosted on Dropbox or similar legitimate hosting
